questions.question: A helmet will give you the most protection if it has all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Fits loosely.
Has no damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits loosely.
questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best when it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve.
Running off the road while trying to avoid another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve.
questions.explanation: Turning too wide in a curve is a main cause of single-vehicle crashes. When you turn too wide, your motorcycle may leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on dry pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and moving straight.

questions.question: Small vehicles like motorcycles appear to be ________ and moving slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast and how far away a small vehicle is. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Stop at the sign or signal and then go normally.
Flash your lights and honk your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where other drivers will see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: You should keep a larger distance between you and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: The road is slippery.
Traffic is light.
You can see through the vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Keep at least a four-second distance behind the vehicle ahead when the road is slippery, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction machinery, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When taking a turn, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: _________ of crashes between motorcycles and cars are caused by the driver not yielding the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers of larger vehicles will yield, even if they are supposed to.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow traffic light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, keep going.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Avoid sudden power changes during the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden power changes during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start turning. Shifting gears while turning can cause a sudden power change to the back wheel, which can cause skidding. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher is considered intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. Anyone who is intoxicated cannot legally drive a motor vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Both brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, position yourself where:

options.text: The driver can see you in the side mirror.
The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
The driver can see you through the passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride behind the car in the center of your lane. This position places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: Can go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always stay within the posted speed limit when passing. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When riding in a group, less experienced riders should be:

options.text: Leading the group.
Near the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Place less experienced riders near the front, right behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the newer riders at the same time.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely need to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure changes.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure settings.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it can tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to improve stability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it can tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip. Use only the rear brake to control your speed during the U-turn.
